transcript.text: panasonic nn h98 not heating anymore, any fix?

For a Panasonic NN-H98 not heating, the most common causes are either an incorrect setting (like Defrost or Low Power) which prevents full heating, or a fault within the high-voltage circuit (such as the magnetron, high-voltage diode, or capacitor). To help narrow this down safely: please check if you were using a low power setting rather than High. Then, try running a cup of water on High for one minute to see if it heats up at all. Please let me know what happens.
[Safety panel] Don't remove the microwave's casing or try to repair it inside. Parts inside a microwave can hold a dangerous electric charge even after it's unplugged — have it checked by a qualified engineer.
its not a low power setting. H98 is what the screen says when it stops; the model on the back is NN-CD87KSBPQ. cup of water stops after about 10-15 secs with H98, water still cold

The H98 code on your Panasonic NN-CD87KSBPQ suggests a high-voltage inverter power fault. Because this is an inverter microwave and the water remained cold after running for 10–15 seconds before stopping, the issue is probably a failed component inside the high-voltage circuit—most likely the inverter board or the magnetron itself. This is not something you can safely fix yourself. Microwaves contain components that store dangerous mains voltage even when unplugged, and diagnosing this requires specialist testing equipment. Please stop using the appliance to avoid any risk of electric shock or fire, and contact a qualified appliance engineer for repair.
